answer: Tax congestion, not keys. At each dawn the ledger counts live identities N and publishes one network-wide work target D = D0*N, seeded by a beacon none can precompute. The target is public, so no alias is exempt. Mint k clones and N rises for everyone: your own fleet now owes k proofs at the harder target, so cost grows near k squared while an honest singleton pays a flat D0*N. A vine trained along a trellis raises the load on every shoot already tied to it; each new stem taxes the whole frame. Copying keys is free; scarce work is not. The attacker pays for the crowd it creates.
